_comment: SHARED CASE TABLE for the board-game lifecycle, read by BOTH runtimes:
A behaviour, not a table, is what these two share — so parity is pinned with
cases rather than by parsing one language from the other (the shape
test_per_side_parity.py uses for a literal list). Drift in either direction
Omitted inputs default: game_id null, the three flags null, captured/restored
false. Each case names only what it is about.

cases.why: a game id and nothing else is a game in progress
absent live_following reads as still following (pre-flag state)
the HUD frame says the game reached its end
the slot holds a completed API record
a parsed box score for THIS game is the strongest evidence, and the only end-of-game signal a HUD board gets
the server stopped following a game that never finished cleanly
final outranks stranded — a result beats an abandonment
restored outranks every detail of a game that is not current
last night's finished game: restored still wins
a mid-game quit reboots restored, not stranded
restored with no game is still empty — the flag describes a game's provenance, not the board

stale._comment: isStaleBoard / is_stale — what has stopped being a game in progress.
